For home emergencies and power outages, I recommend a portable power station with a LiFePO4 (LFP) battery rather than a regular USB power bank.

These can power refrigerators, Wi-Fi routers, lights, laptops, and some household appliances during a blackout.

My starting recommendation is a 2,000 Wh battery for most households that want meaningful emergency backup without installing a permanent whole-home system.

Actual runtime depends on appliance consumption, inverter losses, and battery capacity.

For a 2 kWh battery, expect roughly 7–17 hours at a continuous average load of 100–250 W, allowing for conversion losses. A refrigerator cycles on and off, so actual runtime varies substantially.

Never plug a portable battery into a wall outlet to power house wiring. Use appliances directly or a professionally installed transfer switch.
